name: generic_estimated_22nm
display_name: Generic 22 nm digital IMC (ALL ESTIMATED — not a real chip)

validity.array_size_assumed: 256 x 256 digital SRAM crossbar cores, 8-bit weights
validity.notes: EVERY constant in this profile is an ESTIMATE. It describes no real chip and must never be cited as one. It exists so a first-cut co-optimization study can run before a vendor profile is available, and so the estimated-evidence path is exercised end to end by something a reader cannot mistake for a measurement.

area_per_cell.note: A 6T SRAM bitcell holding one weight bit. Anchored on TrueNorth's published 0.152 um^2 6T cell at 28 nm and scaled by area ~ node^2: 0.152 x (22/28)^2 = 0.094 um^2. The band spans a dense foundry cell (0.05) to a relaxed one (0.16), which is roughly the published spread across vendors at this node. Expected error: a factor of ~2 either way.

area_per_cell_per_weight_bit.note: Digital SRAM storage scales linearly with precision — one bitcell per weight bit — so this equals area_per_cell by construction. Same anchor and same expected error.

e_mac.note: An 8-bit multiply-accumulate. Horowitz (ISSCC 2014) reports ~0.2 pJ for an 8-bit MAC at 45 nm / 0.9 V; scaling energy by ~(22/45) x (0.8/0.9)^2 gives 0.077 pJ. The band's ends are the unscaled 45 nm figure (high) and an aggressively optimized datapath (low). Expected error: a factor of ~2.5.

e_neuron_update.note: One membrane update: read state, accumulate, compare, write back. Anchored between Loihi's published 81 pJ (a large asynchronous core doing far more per update) and a bare 24-bit add at this node (~0.1 pJ), landing an order of magnitude above the arithmetic to account for the state SRAM access that dominates. Expected error: a factor of ~4 — this is the least constrained estimate in the profile.

e_leak_per_neuron_step.note: A leak decrement is a fraction of a full update: one read-modify-write of the same register without the synaptic accumulation, taken as ~10% of e_neuron_update. Expected error: a factor of ~4, inherited from e_neuron_update.

e_intra_tile_packet.note: Delivering one spike packet inside a tile. Bracketed by TrueNorth's published intra-core SRAM-to-controller transport (~47 fJ/bit x 32 bits = 1.5 pJ, the high end) and Loihi's 1.7 pJ within-tile figure, discounted for a shorter digital wire at 22 nm. Expected error: a factor of ~3.

e_inter_tile_hop.note: One packet traversal of one inter-tile link. The band brackets the two published digital points directly: TrueNorth's 2.3 pJ/hop at 28 nm and Loihi's 3.0-4.0 pJ/hop at 14 nm, with the low end allowing a shorter link. Expected error: a factor of ~2.

t_hop.note: Latency of one inter-tile link traversal, bracketing the published digital points (TrueNorth 4 ns, Loihi 4.1-6.5 ns). Not added to end-to-end latency by the pricer — timestep-synchronous execution already contains it — so this constant informs NoC studies only.

t_array_read.note: One 256-row array read. Anchored on typical SRAM macro access times at this node (~1-2 ns) plus accumulation, with the high end allowing a slow multi-bank read. Expected error: a factor of ~3.

t_cycle.note: The timestep period. A DECLARED DESIGN CHOICE rather than a physical limit: the band spans 100 MHz down to 100 kHz timestep rates, and the 1 us nominal is a fast synchronous digital design. Any real target should override this first — it alone converts latency_steps into seconds, so it gates end-to-end latency and throughput entirely.

area_per_neuron_logic.note: Per-neuron update logic, excluding state storage. Anchored on TrueNorth's published 11.328 um^2 per neuron at 28 nm (a 2900 um^2 block time-multiplexed 256 ways) scaled by node^2 to 7.0 um^2, rounded up for a less aggressively multiplexed design. Expected error: a factor of ~3.

area_per_state_bit.note: One bit of membrane state in SRAM — the same bitcell as area_per_cell, so it carries the same anchor, band and expected error.

membrane_bits.note: A 24-bit signed accumulator, matching Loihi's independently characterized width and comfortably above TrueNorth's 20 bits. A design choice rather than a measurement, so it is stated as an estimate.

area_per_router.note: One 5-port mesh router. Typical published NoC router areas at this class of node fall in the low thousands of um^2; the band is wide because buffer depth dominates and no depth is assumed here. Expected error: a factor of ~4.

area_per_tile_fixed.note: Per-tile overhead that is neither array, neuron logic nor router: schedulers, controllers, local buffers. Taken as ~2x the router area, the ratio TrueNorth's core floorplan roughly exhibits. Expected error: a factor of ~4.

area_global_fixed.note: Whole-chip area scaling with neither cores nor tiles: pads, PLLs, host interface. Anchored on TrueNorth's derived 46.6 mm^2 periphery at 28 nm for a 4.3 cm^2 die, scaled down for a smaller die at 22 nm. Expected error: a factor of ~4.

e_dma_per_byte.note: Moving one byte of programming payload onto the chip. This is the framework's own long-standing DMA band (HBM2 ~3.9 pJ/bit, DDR3 ~20 pJ/bit per Horowitz 2014, off-chip worst case) restated per byte, so this profile and the default-band cost model agree on the one coefficient they share.

e_readout_per_byte.note: Moving one byte of pass-boundary emissions OFF the chip. Same off-chip transfer band as e_dma_per_byte (Horowitz 2014 memory-access energy is stated per access, not per direction), restated here so the readout direction is charged explicitly rather than borrowing the inbound constant by omission. A target whose readout path genuinely differs should override this.

bytes_per_connectivity_entry.note: Wire size of one connectivity (axon source span) entry. The framework's declared 4/8/16 B band: span entries are exact counts, but their byte size is modeled until a real chip wire format exists.

e_program_per_byte.derivation: [TS6] Committing one byte into an on-chip SRAM weight store, at Horowitz scale: an 8 KB SRAM 32-bit read is ~5 pJ at 45 nm = 1.25 pJ/B, and scaling by the node ratio 22/45 gives ~0.61 pJ/B of read energy; a write costs about 1-3x a read. A byte written into a wide row amortizes the wordline down toward 0.1 pJ/B, while a narrow byte write into a banked macro reaches 3 pJ/B, so the band is 0.1 - 3.0 pJ/B with the nominal at its log-space centre, sqrt(0.1 x 3.0) = 0.547723 pJ/B. Deliberately NOT anchored on this profile's e_mac: that is an 8-bit datapath multiply, not a memory access.
e_program_per_byte.note: An ESTIMATED exemplar, and the estimated-evidence path's exercise for the programming group. Expected error: a factor of ~5. Distinct from e_dma_per_byte above, which moves the byte onto the chip; this commits it to the array, and a target that declares both pays both.

t_program_per_byte.derivation: The band's ends are two real configuration paths: a wide parallel bus moving about one byte per cycle at a few hundred MHz (4 ns/B) and a serial scan chain like TrueNorth's derived 800 ns/B, rounded to 1000 ns/B at this profile's coarser node, with the nominal assuming a modest dedicated port. Stated as arithmetic because this profile is a DONOR: the targets that publish no configuration rate of their own (loihi, odin, isaac_like) scale this band by validity.technology_node_nm.
t_program_per_byte.note: Wall time to move one programming byte. The band spans a wide parallel configuration bus (4 ns/B) to a slow serial scan chain like TrueNorth's derived 800 ns/B, with a nominal assuming a modest dedicated port. Expected error: two orders of magnitude — this is the widest band in the profile, and deliberately so.

e_core_program.derivation: [TS6] The payload-independent part of a program load, anchored on the core-state SWEEP this profile's own declarations define: 256 neurons per core (validity.array_size_assumed) x e_neuron_update (0.5 / 2.0 / 8.0 pJ) = 128 / 512 / 2048 pJ of per-core control work. The ratio band [0.5x, 2x] is applied to the anchor's own corners, giving 64 - 4096 pJ, with the nominal at the band's log-space centre, sqrt(64 x 4096) = 512 pJ.
e_core_program.note: Six times wider than the device profiles' version of this constant, because it compounds an estimated anchor with the ratio spread - which is exactly what an estimated profile should look like.

e_sync_barrier.note: Energy of one chip-wide synchronization barrier. The framework's existing ~0.1 / ~1 / ~10 uJ band, which no published chip figure contradicts because none exists — Loihi publishes the barrier TIME but not its energy.

t_sync_barrier.note: Wall time of one chip-wide barrier. Anchored directly on Loihi's published 113-465 ns mesh-wide range, with the high end allowing a larger mesh. Expected error: a factor of ~4.

p_static_per_core.note: Static (leakage) power per core. The band brackets the two published digital points — TrueNorth's derived 10.25 uW/core at 28 nm and Loihi's derived 815 uW/core at 14 nm — whose 80x spread is itself the reason this band is wide: leakage depends far more on process flavour and power gating than on node. Expected error: an order of magnitude.

p_static_global.note: Whole-chip leakage outside the cores: I/O ring, PLLs, host interface. Taken as a small fraction of a populated chip's core leakage. Expected error: an order of magnitude.

conductance_levels.note: 8-bit digital weights, the precision this profile's array assumes. A design choice, not a measurement.

write_sigma.note: Zero by the profile's own assumption that the array is DIGITAL SRAM, which has no analog programming spread. Stated as estimated rather than derived because the digital assumption is this profile's premise, not a fact about a real chip.

read_sigma.note: Zero for the same reason as write_sigma: a digital read has no sensing spread.

area_per_adc.note: Zero because this profile assumes a digital array with no analog-to-digital conversion in the datapath. An analog target must declare its own converter area rather than inherit this.

e_adc_conversion.note: Zero for the same digital-array assumption as area_per_adc.

t_adc_conversion.note: Zero for the same digital-array assumption as area_per_adc.

host_compute_rate.derivation: identity: a measured host wall is used at face value (wall / 1.0)
host_compute_rate.note: The derate a MEASURED host wall is divided by. Identity by definition: this framework measures its host ComputeOp walls end-to-end on the deployment host (StageTimer), and derating a measurement would invent headroom. [H5] Declared here after the loihi precedent because its absence refused the record-plane e2e/energy headlines BY NAME on runs whose host wall was in fact measured.
